# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates as human-readable relative time strings.

> *"5 minutes ago" is more useful than "2024-01-15T14:32:00.000Z"*

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — under 1KB minified and gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies** — no bloat, no supply chain risk
- 🌍 **i18n ready** — bring your own locale strings
- ⚡ **Fast** — simple arithmetic, no date parsing magic
- 🔁 **Works everywhere** — ESM, CJS, and browser-ready
- 🧪 **Fully tested** — 100% code coverage

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install tiny-date

# yarn
yarn add tiny-date

# pnpm
pnpm add tiny-date
```

Or use it directly in the browser via CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
```

---

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date());                          // "just now"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 30_000));       // "30 seconds ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000));   // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 3600_000)); // "3 hours ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 86400_000));// "2 days ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 86400_000));// "last month"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 400 * 86400_000));// "last year"
```

---

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing how long ago (or how far in the future) the given date is relative to now.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | ✅ | The date to format. Accepts a `Date` object, a Unix timestamp (ms), or an ISO 8601 string. |
| `options` | `Options` | ❌ | Optional configuration object (see below). |

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `new Date()` | Override the reference point for "now". Useful for testing. |
| `locale` | `Locale` | built-in English | Custom locale strings for i18n support. |
| `future` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to support future dates (e.g., `"in 5 minutes"`). |

#### Returns

`string` — A relative time string.

---

### Time Thresholds

| Elapsed Time | Output |
|---|---|
| < 5 seconds | `"just now"` |
| < 60 seconds | `"30 seconds ago"` |
| < 60 minutes | `"5 minutes ago"` |
| < 24 hours | `"3 hours ago"` |
| < 2 days | `"yesterday"` |
| < 30 days | `"12 days ago"` |
| < 12 months | `"last month"` / `"3 months ago"` |
| ≥ 12 months | `"last year"` / `"2 years ago"` |

---

## Examples

### Basic Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const postDate = new Date('2024-01-10T08:00:00');
console.log(timeAgo(postDate)); // "3 days ago"
```

### Future Dates

```js
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60_000)); // "in 10 minutes"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 86400_000));   // "tomorrow"
```

### Disable Future Dates

```js
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60_000), { future: false });
// "just now"
```

### Custom Reference Point (great for testing)

```js
const base = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00');
const past = new Date('2024-06-01T11:30:00');

timeAgo(past, { now: base }); // "30 minutes ago"
```

### Custom Locale (i18n)

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const es = {
  justNow: 'ahora mismo',
  secondsAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} segundos`,
  minutesAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} minuto${n !== 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  hoursAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} hora${n !== 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  yesterday: 'ayer',
  daysAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} días`,
  lastMonth: 'el mes pasado',
  monthsAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} meses`,
  lastYear: 'el año pasado',
  yearsAgo: (n) => `hace ${n} años`,
  // future keys follow the same pattern
};

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000), { locale: es });
// "hace 5 minutos"
```

---

## TypeScript

`tiny-date` is written in TypeScript and ships with types out of the box — no `@types` package needed.

```ts
import { timeAgo, Options, Locale } from 'tiny-date';

const options: Options = {
  future: true,
  now: new Date(),
};

const result: string = timeAgo(new Date(), options);
```

---

## Browser Support

Works in all modern browsers and Node.js ≥ 14.

| Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Edge | Node.js |
|--------|---------|--------|------|---------|
| ✅ 80+ | ✅ 75+ | ✅ 13+ | ✅ 80+ | ✅ 14+ |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date

# Install dev dependencies
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Build
npm run build
```

---

## Comparison

| Library | Size (min+gz) | Zero deps | TypeScript | i18n |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------|------|
| **tiny-date** | **< 1KB** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| date-fns `formatDistanceToNow` | ~18KB | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| moment.js `fromNow` | ~72KB | ❌ | ⚠️ | ✅ |
| timeago.js | ~3KB | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © 2024 Your Name

---

*If `tiny-date` saves you time, consider giving it a ⭐ on [GitHub](https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date)!*

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates as human-readable relative time strings.

> *"5 minutes ago" is more useful than "2024-01-15T14:32:00.000Z"*

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — under 1KB minified + gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies**
- 🌐 **Works everywhere** — Node.js, browsers, and edge runtimes
- 🕐 **Smart formatting** — from seconds to years
- 🔁 **Future dates** — supports "in 5 minutes" style output
- 🧩 **TypeScript support** — ships with built-in types
- ✅ **Well tested** — 100% test coverage

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install tiny-date

# yarn
yarn add tiny-date

# pnpm
pnpm add tiny-date
```

Or use it directly in the browser via CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
```

---

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date());                          // "just now"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 30_000));       // "30 seconds ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000));   // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 3_600_000));// "2 hours ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 86_400_000));// "3 days ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 60_000));       // "in 1 minute"
```

---

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Formats a `Date` object (or timestamp) relative to the current time.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | ✅ | The date to format |
| `options` | `TimeAgoOptions` | ❌ | Optional configuration |

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `new Date()` | Override the reference "now" time |
| `max` | `number` | `Infinity` | Max milliseconds before falling back to `fallback` |
| `fallback` | `string \| function` | `undefined` | String or formatter to use when `max` is exceeded |

#### Returns

`string` — A human-readable relative time string.

---

## Examples

### Basic Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

// Past dates
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5000));         // "5 seconds ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 90_000));       // "1 minute ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 45 * 60_000)); // "45 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 36_000_000));  // "10 hours ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 86_400_000));  // "yesterday"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 14 * 86_400_000)); // "2 weeks ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 365 * 86_400_000)); // "1 year ago"

// Future dates
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 5000));         // "in 5 seconds"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 3_600_000));    // "in 1 hour"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 86_400_000)); // "in 7 days"
```

### Using a Custom Reference Time

```js
const past = new Date('2020-01-01');
const reference = new Date('2020-06-01');

timeAgo(past, { now: reference }); // "5 months ago"
```

### Fallback for Old Dates

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const oneWeekMs = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

// Use a static fallback string
timeAgo(new Date('2019-01-01'), {
  max: oneWeekMs,
  fallback: 'a long time ago',
}); // "a long time ago"

// Use a custom formatter function
timeAgo(new Date('2019-03-15'), {
  max: oneWeekMs,
  fallback: (date) => date.toLocaleDateString(),
}); // "3/15/2019"
```

### Accepts Multiple Input Types

```js
timeAgo(new Date('2024-01-01'));   // Date object
timeAgo(1704067200000);            // Unix timestamp (ms)
timeAgo('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z');  // ISO string
```

---

## Time Scale Reference

| Elapsed Time | Output |
|---|---|
| 0 – 4 seconds | `"just now"` |
| 5 – 59 seconds | `"N seconds ago"` |
| 60s – 89s | `"1 minute ago"` |
| 90s – 59 minutes | `"N minutes ago"` |
| 1 – 21 hours | `"N hours ago"` |
| 22 – 35 hours | `"yesterday"` |
| 36 hours – 25 days | `"N days ago"` |
| 26 – 45 days | `"1 month ago"` |
| 46 days – 10 months | `"N months ago"` |
| 11 – 17 months | `"1 year ago"` |
| 18+ months | `"N years ago"` |

> Future dates follow the same scale with `"in ..."` prefix.

---

## CommonJS Usage

```js
const { timeAgo } = require('tiny-date');

console.log(timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 60_000))); // "1 minute ago"
```

---

## TypeScript

`tiny-date` ships with full TypeScript definitions — no `@types` package needed.

```ts
import { timeAgo, type TimeAgoOptions } from 'tiny-date';

const options: TimeAgoOptions = {
  max: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
  fallback: (date: Date) => date.toISOString(),
};

const result: string = timeAgo(new Date(), options);
```

---

## Browser Support

| Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Edge | Node.js |
|--------|---------|--------|------|---------|
| ✅ 60+ | ✅ 55+ | ✅ 12+ | ✅ 79+ | ✅ 14+ |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date

# Install dev dependencies
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Build
npm run build
```

Please make sure all tests pass and coverage remains at 100% before opening a PR.

---

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © Your Name

---

## Related Projects

- [date-fns](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns) — Full-featured date utility library
- [dayjs](https://github.com/iamkun/dayjs) — Lightweight Moment.js alternative
- [timeago.js](https://github.com/hustcc/timeago.js) — Similar library with i18n support

> **tiny-date** is for you if you *only* need relative formatting and want the smallest possible footprint.

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates as human-readable relative time strings.

> *"5 minutes ago" is more useful than "2024-01-15T14:32:00.000Z"*

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — under 1KB minified + gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies** — no bloat, no supply chain risk
- 🌍 **i18n ready** — bring your own locale strings
- ⚡ **Fast** — simple arithmetic, no heavy date parsing
- 🔁 **Works everywhere** — ESM, CJS, and browser-ready
- 🧪 **Fully tested** — 100% code coverage

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install tiny-date

# yarn
yarn add tiny-date

# pnpm
pnpm add tiny-date
```

Or use it directly in the browser via CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
```

---

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date());                          // "just now"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 30_000));       // "30 seconds ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000));   // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 3600_000)); // "3 hours ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 86400_000));// "2 days ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 8 * 86400_000));// "1 week ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 86400_000));// "2 months ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 400 * 86400_000));// "1 year ago"
```

---

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Returns a human-readable string describing how long ago (or how far in the future) the given date is relative to now.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number \| string` | ✅ | The date to format. Accepts a `Date` object, a Unix timestamp (ms), or an ISO 8601 string. |
| `options` | `Options` | ❌ | Optional configuration object (see below). |

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `new Date()` | Override the reference point for "now". Useful for testing. |
| `locale` | `Locale` | built-in English | Custom locale strings for i18n support. |
| `future` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to support future dates (e.g., `"in 3 hours"`). |

#### Returns

`string` — A relative time string.

#### Examples

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

// Basic usage
timeAgo('2024-01-10T10:00:00Z');
// → "3 days ago"

// Using a Unix timestamp
timeAgo(1705483200000);
// → "2 days ago"

// Future dates
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60_000));
// → "in 10 minutes"

// Disable future support
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 10 * 60_000), { future: false });
// → "just now"

// Override "now" (great for testing)
timeAgo(new Date('2024-01-01'), { now: new Date('2024-01-06') });
// → "5 days ago"
```

---

## Time Thresholds

| Elapsed Time | Output |
|---|---|
| < 5 seconds | `"just now"` |
| < 60 seconds | `"N seconds ago"` |
| < 60 minutes | `"N minutes ago"` |
| < 24 hours | `"N hours ago"` |
| < 7 days | `"N days ago"` |
| < 30 days | `"N weeks ago"` |
| < 12 months | `"N months ago"` |
| ≥ 12 months | `"N years ago"` |

Future dates follow the same thresholds but are prefixed with `"in"` (e.g., `"in 2 hours"`).

---

## Internationalization (i18n)

Pass a custom `locale` object to render output in any language.

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const fr = {
  justNow: "à l'instant",
  past: (value) => `il y a ${value}`,
  future: (value) => `dans ${value}`,
  seconds: (n) => `${n} secondes`,
  minutes: (n) => `${n} minute${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  hours:   (n) => `${n} heure${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  days:    (n) => `${n} jour${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  weeks:   (n) => `${n} semaine${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  months:  (n) => `${n} mois`,
  years:   (n) => `${n} an${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
};

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000), { locale: fr });
// → "il y a 5 minutes"
```

---

## Usage with Frameworks

### React

```jsx
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

function Timestamp({ date }) {
  return (
    <time dateTime={date.toISOString()} title={date.toLocaleString()}>
      {timeAgo(date)}
    </time>
  );
}

// <Timestamp date={new Date(Date.now() - 120_000)} />
// → <time ...>2 minutes ago</time>
```

### Vue

```vue
<template>
  <time :datetime="date.toISOString()">{{ relative }}</time>
</template>

<script setup>
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const props = defineProps({ date: Date });
const relative = computed(() => timeAgo(props.date));
</script>
```

---

## TypeScript

`tiny-date` ships with full TypeScript definitions out of the box.

```ts
import { timeAgo, type Options, type Locale } from 'tiny-date';

const options: Options = {
  now: new Date(),
  future: true,
};

const result: string = timeAgo(new Date(), options);
```

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date

# Install dev dependencies
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Build
npm run build
```

Please make sure all tests pass and coverage remains at 100% before submitting a PR.

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © 2024 Your Name

---

## Alternatives

If `tiny-date` doesn't fit your needs, check out:

- [**date-fns** `formatDistanceToNow`](https://date-fns.org/) — full-featured date utility library
- [**dayjs** `fromNow`](https://day.js.org/) — lightweight Moment.js alternative
- [**Intl.RelativeTimeFormat**](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/RelativeTimeFormat) — native browser API (no library needed!)

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates relative to the current time.

> *"5 minutes ago" · "in 3 days" · "just now"*

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — under 1KB minified and gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies** — no bloat, no surprises
- 🌍 **i18n ready** — bring your own locale strings
- ⚙️ **Configurable** — customize thresholds and output
- 🟦 **TypeScript support** — ships with type definitions
- 🌐 **Universal** — works in Node.js and the browser

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install tiny-date

# yarn
yarn add tiny-date

# pnpm
pnpm add tiny-date
```

Or use it directly in the browser via CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
```

---

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date());                          // "just now"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000));  // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 86_400_000)); // "in 3 days"
```

---

## Usage

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Accepts a `Date` object, a timestamp (`number`), or an ISO date string and returns a human-readable relative string.

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

// All of these are valid inputs
timeAgo(new Date('2024-01-15'));
timeAgo(1705276800000);
timeAgo('2024-01-15T00:00:00Z');
```

#### Output Examples

| Time Difference     | Output               |
|---------------------|----------------------|
| 0 – 10 seconds      | `"just now"`         |
| 45 seconds ago      | `"45 seconds ago"`   |
| 5 minutes ago       | `"5 minutes ago"`    |
| 1 hour ago          | `"1 hour ago"`       |
| 3 days ago          | `"3 days ago"`       |
| 2 weeks ago         | `"2 weeks ago"`      |
| 6 months ago        | `"6 months ago"`     |
| 2 years ago         | `"2 years ago"`      |
| in 10 minutes       | `"in 10 minutes"`    |
| in 1 year           | `"in 1 year"`        |

---

## Options

```js
timeAgo(date, {
  now:       Date.now(),  // Reference timestamp (default: current time)
  max:       null,        // Max age in ms before returning null (default: none)
  locale:    defaultLocale, // Custom locale strings (see Localization)
  suffix:    true,        // Include "ago" / "in" framing (default: true)
})
```

### `now`

Override the reference point for "now". Useful for testing or server-side rendering.

```js
const fixedNow = new Date('2024-06-01T12:00:00Z').getTime();

timeAgo('2024-06-01T11:55:00Z', { now: fixedNow });
// "5 minutes ago"
```

### `max`

Return `null` if the date is older than a given number of milliseconds. Useful when you want to fall back to an absolute date format beyond a certain age.

```js
const ONE_WEEK = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const result = timeAgo(oldDate, { max: ONE_WEEK });

if (result === null) {
  // Fall back to absolute date
  console.log(oldDate.toLocaleDateString());
} else {
  console.log(result); // "3 days ago"
}
```

### `suffix`

Disable the `"ago"` / `"in"` framing to get just the duration.

```js
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000), { suffix: false });
// "5 minutes"
```

---

## Localization

Pass a custom `locale` object to render output in any language.

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const fr = {
  justNow:   'à l\'instant',
  past:      (v) => `il y a ${v}`,
  future:    (v) => `dans ${v}`,
  second:    (n) => `${n} seconde${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  minute:    (n) => `${n} minute${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  hour:      (n) => `${n} heure${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  day:       (n) => `${n} jour${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  week:      (n) => `${n} semaine${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  month:     (n) => `${n} mois`,
  year:      (n) => `${n} an${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
};

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000), { locale: fr });
// "il y a 5 minutes"
```

Community locale packs will be listed in the [Wiki](../../wiki).

---

## TypeScript

`tiny-date` ships with full TypeScript definitions.

```ts
import { timeAgo, TinyDateOptions, TinyDateLocale } from 'tiny-date';

const options: TinyDateOptions = {
  max: 604_800_000,
  locale: myLocale,
};

const result: string | null = timeAgo(new Date(), options);
```

---

## API Reference

| Function | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `timeAgo` | `date: Date \| number \| string, options?: TinyDateOptions` | `string \| null` |

---

## Browser Support

Works in all modern browsers and Node.js ≥ 14.

| Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Edge | Node.js |
|--------|---------|--------|------|---------|
| ✅ 60+ | ✅ 60+  | ✅ 12+ | ✅ 79+ | ✅ 14+ |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date

# Install dev dependencies
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Build
npm run build
```

Please make sure all tests pass and new features include test coverage.

---

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © Your Name

---

## Similar Projects

If `tiny-date` isn't quite what you need, check out these alternatives:

- [**day.js**](https://day.js.org/) — full-featured date library
- [**date-fns**](https://date-fns.org/) — modular date utilities
- [**timeago.js**](https://timeago.org/) — similar focus, larger API

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. ```bash # Clone and install git clone https://github.com/yourname/tiny-date.git cd tiny-date npm install # Run tests npm test # Build npm run build ``` Please make sure your PR: - [ ] Includes tests for any new behaviour - [ ] Does not increase the minified bundle size beyond **1KB** - [ ] Updates the README if the API changes --- ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2024 Your Name ---

If you find this useful, consider giving it a ⭐ on GitHub!

# tiny-date

A lightweight, zero-dependency JavaScript library for formatting dates as human-readable relative time strings.

> *"5 minutes ago" · "in 3 days" · "just now"*

---

## Features

- 🪶 **Tiny** — under 1KB minified and gzipped
- 🚫 **Zero dependencies** — no bloat, no surprises
- 🌐 **Universal** — works in Node.js and the browser
- 🔷 **TypeScript-ready** — ships with built-in type definitions
- 🌍 **i18n-friendly** — bring your own locale strings
- ⚡ **Simple API** — one function, sensible defaults

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install tiny-date

# yarn
yarn add tiny-date

# pnpm
pnpm add tiny-date
```

Or use it directly in the browser via CDN:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-date/dist/tiny-date.min.js"></script>
```

---

## Quick Start

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

timeAgo(new Date());                          // "just now"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 30_000));       // "30 seconds ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000));   // "5 minutes ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 3_600_000));// "2 hours ago"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 86_400_000));   // "in 1 day"
timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 86_400_000)); // "in 7 days"
```

---

## API

### `timeAgo(date, options?)`

Formats a `Date` object (or a Unix timestamp in milliseconds) relative to the current time.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `Date \| number` | ✅ | The date to format |
| `options` | `TimeAgoOptions` | ❌ | Optional configuration object |

#### Returns

`string` — A human-readable relative time string.

#### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `now` | `Date \| number` | `new Date()` | Override the reference point for "now" |
| `labels` | `Labels` | `en` built-in | Custom label strings for localization |
| `max` | `number` | `undefined` | Max seconds before falling back to `fallback` |
| `fallback` | `string \| function` | `undefined` | Value returned when `max` is exceeded |

---

## Examples

### Basic Usage

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const post = { createdAt: new Date('2024-01-15T10:30:00Z') };

console.log(timeAgo(post.createdAt)); // e.g. "3 months ago"
```

### Custom Reference Time

Useful for testing or server-side rendering with a fixed timestamp.

```js
timeAgo(new Date('2024-06-01'), {
  now: new Date('2024-06-03'),
}); // "2 days ago"
```

### Max Threshold with Fallback

Fall back to an absolute date string after a certain point.

```js
timeAgo(new Date('2020-01-01'), {
  max: 60 * 60 * 24 * 30, // 30 days in seconds
  fallback: (date) => date.toLocaleDateString(),
}); // "1/1/2020"
```

### Custom Labels (i18n)

```js
import { timeAgo } from 'tiny-date';

const frenchLabels = {
  justNow:  'à l\'instant',
  past:     (v) => `il y a ${v}`,
  future:   (v) => `dans ${v}`,
  seconds:  (n) => `${n} secondes`,
  minutes:  (n) => `${n} minute${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  hours:    (n) => `${n} heure${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  days:     (n) => `${n} jour${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  weeks:    (n) => `${n} semaine${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
  months:   (n) => `${n} mois`,
  years:    (n) => `${n} an${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`,
};

timeAgo(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000), {
  labels: frenchLabels,
}); // "il y a 5 minutes"
```

---

## Time Ranges

| Elapsed Time | Output |
|---|---|
| 0 – 10 seconds | `just now` |
| 11 – 59 seconds | `N seconds ago` |
| 1 – 59 minutes | `N minutes ago` |
| 1 – 23 hours | `N hours ago` |
| 1 – 6 days | `N days ago` |
| 1 – 3 weeks | `N weeks ago` |
| 1 – 11 months | `N months ago` |
| 12+ months | `N years ago` |

Future dates follow the same intervals with `in N ...` formatting.

---

## TypeScript

`tiny-date` is written in TypeScript and ships with full type definitions.

```ts
import { timeAgo, TimeAgoOptions, Labels } from 'tiny-date';

const options: TimeAgoOptions = {
  now: new Date(),
  max: 86_400,
  fallback: (date: Date) => date.toISOString(),
};

const result: string = timeAgo(new Date(), options);
```

---

## Browser Support

Works in all modern browsers and any environment that supports **ES2017+**.
For older environments, include a `Date` polyfill and transpile with Babel.

| Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Edge | Node.js |
|--------|---------|--------|------|---------|
| ✅ 60+ | ✅ 55+ | ✅ 12+ | ✅ 79+ | ✅ 12+ |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-username/tiny-date.git
cd tiny-date

# Install dev dependencies
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Build
npm run build
```

---

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2024 Your Name

---

## Related Projects

- [`date-fns`](https://date-fns.org/) — full-featured date utility library
- [`dayjs`](https://day.js.org/) — lightweight Moment.js alternative
- [`timeago.js`](https://timeago.org/) — similar library with more locales

> **tiny-date** is for when you *only* need relative formatting and every byte counts.

runs.output:
# flak

A fast, lightweight CLI tool for linting YAML files.

---

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Options & Flags](#options--flags)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Examples](#examples)
- [Exit Codes](#exit-codes)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Overview

**flak** is a command-line linter for YAML files. It helps you catch syntax errors, enforce formatting conventions, and maintain consistency across your YAML configurations — whether they're CI pipelines, Kubernetes manifests, Docker Compose files, or anything else.

---

## Installation

### Using npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Using Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Using cargo

```bash
cargo install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

---

## Usage

```bash
flak [OPTIONS] <FILE|GLOB...>
```

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files:

```bash
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Lint using a glob pattern:

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml"
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak -
```

---

## Options & Flags

| Flag                        | Description                                              | Default     |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <file>`       | Path to a custom configuration file                      | `.flak.yml` |
| `-f, --format <format>`     | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `compact`, `github`     | `pretty`    |
| `-o, --output <file>`       | Write output to a file instead of stdout                 | —           |
| `--fix`                     | Automatically fix auto-fixable issues                    | `false`     |
| `--ignore <pattern>`        | Glob pattern of files to ignore (repeatable)             | —           |
| `--no-color`                | Disable colored output                                   | `false`     |
| `--max-warnings <n>`        | Exit with error if warnings exceed this number           | —           |
| `-q, --quiet`               | Only report errors, suppress warnings                    | `false`     |
| `-s, --strict`              | Treat warnings as errors                                 | `false`     |
| `--stdin-filename <name>`   | Virtual filename to use when reading from stdin          | `stdin`     |
| `-v, --verbose`             | Show detailed output including passing checks            | `false`     |
| `--version`                 | Print the current version                                | —           |
| `-h, --help`                | Show help information                                    | —           |

---

## Configuration

flak looks for a configuration file in the following order:

1. Path specified by `--config`
2. `.flak.yml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.yml` in the user's home directory

### Example `.flak.yml`

```yaml
# .flak.yml

extends: default        # Start from the built-in default ruleset

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"
  - "tests/fixtures/**"

rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
    indent-sequences: true

  trailing-spaces:
    enabled: true

  line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120

  truthy:
    enabled: true
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]

  empty-lines:
    enabled: true
    max: 1
    max-start: 0
    max-end: 1

  comments:
    enabled: true
    require-starting-space: true
    min-spaces-from-content: 2

  key-duplicates:
    enabled: true

  new-line-at-end-of-file:
    enabled: true
```

---

## Rules

flak ships with the following built-in rules:

| Rule                        | Description                                                  | Auto-fix |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
| `indentation`               | Enforce consistent indentation width                         | ✅        |
| `trailing-spaces`           | Disallow trailing whitespace on lines                        | ✅        |
| `line-length`               | Enforce a maximum line length                                | ❌        |
| `truthy`                    | Restrict accepted values for boolean-like fields             | ❌        |
| `empty-lines`               | Limit consecutive empty lines                                | ✅        |
| `comments`                  | Enforce comment formatting conventions                       | ✅        |
| `key-duplicates`            | Disallow duplicate keys in mappings                          | ❌        |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file`   | Require a newline at the end of every file                   | ✅        |
| `document-start`            | Require or forbid the `---` document start marker            | ✅        |
| `document-end`              | Require or forbid the `...` document end marker              | ✅        |
| `quoted-strings`            | Enforce quoting style for string values                      | ❌        |
| `octal-values`              | Warn on ambiguous octal literals (e.g. `0777`)               | ❌        |
| `float-values`              | Warn on ambiguous float representations                      | ❌        |
| `brackets`                  | Control spaces inside flow sequence brackets                 | ✅        |
| `braces`                    | Control spaces inside flow mapping braces                    | ✅        |
| `colons`                    | Enforce spacing around colons                                | ✅        |
| `commas`                    | Enforce spacing around commas in flow collections            | ✅        |

> **Note:** Rules marked ✅ under *Auto-fix* can be resolved automatically with the `--fix` flag.

---

## Examples

**Lint all YAML files in a project:**

```bash
flak "**/*.yml" "**/*.yaml"
```

**Lint with JSON output for tooling integration:**

```bash
flak --format json config.yaml
```

**Auto-fix fixable issues:**

```bash
flak --fix "**/*.yaml"
```

**Strict mode — fail on any warning:**

```bash
flak --strict deployment.yaml
```

**Use a custom config file:**

```bash
flak --config ./ci/.flak.yml pipeline.yaml
```

**Ignore specific paths:**

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml" --ignore "vendor/**" --ignore "dist/**"
```

**Pipe output to a file:**

```bash
flak --format json "**/*.yaml" --output lint-report.json
```

**GitHub Actions annotation format:**

```bash
flak --format github "**/*.yaml"
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                      |
|------|----------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | No errors found                              |
| `1`  | One or more linting errors found             |
| `2`  | Too many warnings (see `--max-warnings`)     |
| `3`  | Invalid configuration file                   |
| `4`  | No files matched the provided pattern        |
| `5`  | Unexpected internal error                    |

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak

# Install dependencies
make setup

# Run tests
make test

# Run flak on itself
make lint
```

Please make sure all tests pass and new rules include corresponding test fixtures.

---

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © your-org

# flak

A fast, lightweight CLI tool for linting YAML files.

## Features

- Validate YAML syntax and structure
- Detect common formatting issues
- Support for single files, multiple files, and glob patterns
- Configurable rules via a `.flak.yml` config file
- Exit codes suitable for use in CI/CD pipelines
- Colorized terminal output

---

## Installation

### Using npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Using Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

---

## Usage

```
flak [options] <file|glob...>
```

### Examples

```bash
# Lint a single file
flak config.yml

# Lint multiple files
flak config.yml docker-compose.yml

# Lint all YAML files in a directory
flak "src/**/*.yml"

# Lint with a custom config file
flak --config .flak.yml "**/*.yaml"

# Output results as JSON
flak --format json config.yml

# Suppress all output (exit code only)
flak --quiet config.yml
```

---

## Options

| Option | Alias | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config <path>` | `-c` | Path to a config file | `.flak.yml` |
| `--format <type>` | `-f` | Output format (`text`, `json`, `compact`) | `text` |
| `--quiet` | `-q` | Suppress output, return exit code only | `false` |
| `--no-color` | | Disable colorized output | `false` |
| `--max-warnings <n>` | | Fail if warnings exceed this number | `∞` |
| `--ignore <glob>` | | Glob pattern of files to ignore | — |
| `--fix` | | Automatically fix fixable issues | `false` |
| `--version` | `-v` | Print the current version | — |
| `--help` | `-h` | Show help information | — |

---

## Rules

flak comes with a set of built-in rules. Each rule can be set to `error`, `warn`, or `off`.

| Rule | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `indentation` | Enforce consistent indentation | `error` |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallow trailing whitespace | `error` |
| `new-line-at-end` | Require a newline at end of file | `warn` |
| `quotes` | Enforce consistent quote style | `warn` |
| `truthy` | Disallow ambiguous truthy values (e.g. `yes`, `on`) | `warn` |
| `line-length` | Enforce a maximum line length | `warn` |
| `empty-lines` | Limit consecutive empty lines | `warn` |
| `key-duplicates` | Disallow duplicate keys | `error` |
| `comments-indentation` | Enforce consistent comment indentation | `off` |

---

## Configuration

Create a `.flak.yml` file in your project root to customize behavior.

```yaml
# .flak.yml

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 120
  quotes:
    level: warn
    preferred: double
  truthy:
    level: error
  trailing-spaces: error
  key-duplicates: error
  new-line-at-end: off
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | One or more linting errors found |
| `2` | Too many warnings (see `--max-warnings`) |
| `3` | Invalid configuration or CLI usage error |

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML files
```

```yaml
repos:
```

# flak

A fast, lightweight CLI tool for linting YAML files.

---

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Options & Flags](#options--flags)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Examples](#examples)
- [Exit Codes](#exit-codes)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Overview

**flak** is a command-line linter for YAML files. It helps you catch syntax errors, enforce formatting conventions, and maintain consistency across your YAML configurations — whether you're working with Docker Compose files, Kubernetes manifests, CI/CD pipelines, or any other YAML-based configuration.

---

## Installation

### Using npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Using Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Using cargo

```bash
cargo install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

---

## Usage

```bash
flak [options] <file|glob...>
```

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files:

```bash
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Lint using a glob pattern:

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml"
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin
```

---

## Options & Flags

| Flag                        | Description                                              | Default     |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <path>`       | Path to a custom configuration file                      | `.flak.yml` |
| `-r, --rules <rules...>`    | Enable specific rules (comma-separated)                  | all rules   |
| `--ignore <pattern>`        | Glob pattern of files to ignore                          | —           |
| `--stdin`                   | Read YAML input from stdin                               | `false`     |
| `--fix`                     | Automatically fix fixable issues                         | `false`     |
| `-f, --format <format>`     | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `compact`, `github`     | `pretty`    |
| `-q, --quiet`               | Only report errors, suppress warnings                    | `false`     |
| `--no-color`                | Disable colored output                                   | `false`     |
| `--max-warnings <number>`   | Fail if warnings exceed this threshold                   | —           |
| `-v, --version`             | Print the current version                                | —           |
| `-h, --help`                | Show help information                                    | —           |

---

## Configuration

flak looks for a configuration file in the following order:

1. Path specified by `--config`
2. `.flak.yml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.yml` in the home directory (`~/.flak.yml`)

### Example `.flak.yml`

```yaml
# .flak.yml

ignore:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
  trailing-spaces:
    enabled: true
  line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120
  quotes:
    enabled: true
    prefer: double
  empty-lines:
    enabled: true
    max-consecutive: 2
  key-duplicates:
    enabled: true
  truthy:
    enabled: true
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  comments:
    enabled: false
```

---

## Rules

| Rule                | Description                                              | Fixable |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `indentation`       | Enforces consistent indentation (spaces, not tabs)       | ✅      |
| `trailing-spaces`   | Disallows trailing whitespace on lines                   | ✅      |
| `line-length`       | Enforces a maximum line length                           | ❌      |
| `quotes`            | Enforces consistent use of single or double quotes       | ✅      |
| `empty-lines`       | Limits consecutive blank lines                           | ✅      |
| `key-duplicates`    | Disallows duplicate keys in a mapping                    | ❌      |
| `truthy`            | Enforces explicit boolean values (`true`/`false`)        | ✅      |
| `document-start`    | Requires or forbids a `---` document start marker        | ✅      |
| `new-line-at-eof`   | Requires a newline at the end of the file                | ✅      |
| `comments`          | Enforces a space after the `#` in comments              | ✅      |
| `octal-values`      | Warns about ambiguous octal-like values (e.g. `0777`)    | ❌      |

---

## Examples

### Basic lint with pretty output

```bash
$ flak config.yaml

config.yaml
  3:5   error    duplicate key "name"              key-duplicates
  7:1   warning  line exceeds 120 characters       line-length
 12:3   error    wrong indentation (4 spaces)      indentation

✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)
```

### Auto-fix fixable issues

```bash
flak --fix "**/*.yaml"
```

### Output as JSON (useful for CI pipelines)

```bash
flak --format json config.yaml
```

```json
{
  "file": "config.yaml",
  "errors": 2,
  "warnings": 1,
  "messages": [
    {
      "line": 3,
      "col": 5,
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "duplicate key \"name\"",
      "rule": "key-duplicates"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Use with GitHub Actions

```bash
flak --format github "**/*.yaml"
```

### Lint and fail if there are more than 5 warnings

```bash
flak --max-warnings 5 "**/*.yaml"
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                      |
|------|----------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | No errors found                              |
| `1`  | One or more linting errors found             |
| `2`  | Warning threshold exceeded (`--max-warnings`)|
| `3`  | Invalid configuration or bad CLI arguments   |

# flak

A fast, lightweight CLI tool for linting YAML files.

## Features

- Validate YAML syntax and structure
- Detect common formatting issues
- Configurable rules via a config file
- Support for single files, multiple files, and glob patterns
- Exit codes suitable for use in CI/CD pipelines

## Installation

### Using npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Using Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

## Usage

```bash
flak [options] <file|glob>
```

### Examples

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files:

```bash
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml
```

Lint all YAML files in a directory:

```bash
flak "src/**/*.yaml"
```

Lint from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin
```

## Options

| Flag | Short | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--help` | `-h` | Show help information |
| `--version` | `-v` | Show the current version |
| `--config <path>` | `-c` | Path to a config file (default: `.flak.yaml`) |
| `--format <type>` | `-f` | Output format: `text`, `json`, `github` (default: `text`) |
| `--stdin` | | Read YAML from stdin |
| `--quiet` | `-q` | Only output errors, suppress warnings |
| `--no-color` | | Disable colored output |
| `--fix` | | Automatically fix fixable issues |

## Output

By default, `flak` outputs results in a human-readable format:

```
config.yaml
  3:5  error    unexpected key "nmae"          no-unknown-keys
  7:1  warning  trailing whitespace detected   no-trailing-spaces
 12:3  error    duplicate key "timeout"        no-duplicate-keys

docker-compose.yml
  1:1  warning  missing document start "---"   require-document-start

4 problems (2 errors, 2 warnings)
```

### JSON output

Use `--format json` for machine-readable output:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "config.yaml",
      "issues": [
        {
          "line": 3,
          "column": 5,
          "severity": "error",
          "message": "unexpected key \"nmae\"",
          "rule": "no-unknown-keys"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "errors": 1,
    "warnings": 0,
    "files": 1
  }
}
```

## Configuration

Create a `.flak.yaml` file in your project root to customize linting rules:

```yaml
# .flak.yaml

extends: default  # Use the default ruleset as a base

rules:
  # Enforce consistent indentation (2 spaces)
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2

  # Disallow duplicate keys
  no-duplicate-keys:
    enabled: true
    severity: error

  # Require a document start marker (---)
  require-document-start:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning

  # Disallow trailing whitespace
  no-trailing-spaces:
    enabled: true

  # Enforce consistent line endings
  line-endings:
    enabled: true
    type: unix  # "unix" (LF) or "windows" (CRLF)

  # Limit line length
  max-line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120

ignore:
  - vendor/**
  - "*.generated.yaml"
```

### Extending configs

You can extend a shared or built-in config:

```yaml
extends:
  - default
  - ./shared/.flak.yaml
```

Built-in configs:

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `default` | Sensible defaults for most projects |
| `strict` | Stricter rules, all warnings become errors |
| `relaxed` | Minimal rules, only hard errors |

## Rules

| Rule | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `indentation` | `error` | Enforce consistent indentation |
| `no-duplicate-keys` | `error` | Disallow duplicate keys in a mapping |
| `no-trailing-spaces` | `warning` | Disallow trailing whitespace |
| `require-document-start` | `off` | Require `---` at the start of a document |
| `max-line-length` | `warning` | Enforce a maximum line length |
| `no-tabs` | `error` | Disallow tab characters for indentation |
| `line-endings` | `warning` | Enforce consistent line endings |
| `truthy` | `warning` | Enforce consistent use of truthy values |
| `empty-lines` | `warning` | Limit the number of consecutive empty lines |
| `key-ordering` | `off` | Enforce alphabetical key ordering |

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | One or more linting errors found |
| `2` | Invalid configuration or unexpected runtime error |

## Ignoring Files

Add a `.flakignore` file to your project root to exclude files and directories:

```
vendor/
node_modules/
*.generated.yaml
secrets.yaml
```

You can also ignore specific lines inline:

```yaml
# flak-disable-next-line no-duplicate-keys
key: value
```

Or disable rules for an entire file by adding a comment at the top:

```yaml
# flak-disable require-document-start
```

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML files
  run: |
    npm install -g flak
    flak --format github "**/*.yaml"
```

### Pre-commit hook

Add `flak` to your `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        name: Lint YAML files
        entry: flak
        language: system
        types: [yaml]
```

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a pull request.

1. Fork the repository
2. Create a feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/my-feature`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'Add my feature'`)
4. Push to the branch (`git push origin feature/my-feature`)
5. Open a pull request

| Flag                        | Description                                              | Default     |

```yaml
extends: default        # Start from the built-in default ruleset

ignore:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"
  - "tests/fixtures/**"

rules:

    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
```

## Overview

**flak** is a command-line linter for YAML files. It helps you catch syntax errors, enforce formatting conventions, and maintain consistency across your YAML configurations — whether you're working with Docker Compose files, Kubernetes manifests, CI/CD pipelines, or any other YAML-based configuration.

---

## Installation

### Using npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### Using Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### Using cargo

```bash
cargo install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

---

## Usage

```bash
flak [options] <file|glob...>
```

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files:

```bash
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Lint using a glob pattern:

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml"
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin
```

---

## Options & Flags

| Flag                        | Description                                              | Default     |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `-c, --config <path>`       | Path to a custom configuration file                      | `.flak.yml` |
| `-r, --rules <rules...>`    | Enable specific rules (comma-separated)                  | all rules   |
| `--ignore <pattern>`        | Glob pattern of files to ignore                          | —           |
| `--stdin`                   | Read YAML input from stdin                               | `false`     |
| `--fix`                     | Automatically fix fixable issues                         | `false`     |
| `-f, --format <format>`     | Output format: `pretty`, `json`, `compact`, `github`     | `pretty`    |
| `-q, --quiet`               | Only report errors, suppress warnings                    | `false`     |
| `--no-color`                | Disable colored output                                   | `false`     |
| `--max-warnings <number>`   | Fail if warnings exceed this threshold                   | —           |
| `-v, --version`             | Print the current version                                | —           |
| `-h, --help`                | Show help information                                    | —           |

---

## Configuration

flak looks for a configuration file in the following order:

1. Path specified via `--config`
2. `.flak.yml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.yml` in the home directory (`~/.flak.yml`)

### Example `.flak.yml`

```yaml
# .flak.yml

ignore:
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "vendor/**"
  - "*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    spaces: 2
  trailing-spaces:
    enabled: true
  line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120
  quotes:
    enabled: true
    prefer: double
  empty-lines:
    enabled: true
    max-consecutive: 2
  key-duplicates:
    enabled: true
  truthy:
    enabled: true
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  comments:
    enabled: false
```

---

## Rules

| Rule                | Description                                              | Fixable |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `indentation`       | Enforces consistent indentation (spaces, not tabs)       | ✅      |
| `trailing-spaces`   | Disallows trailing whitespace on lines                   | ✅      |
| `line-length`       | Enforces a maximum line length                           | ❌      |
| `quotes`            | Enforces consistent use of single or double quotes       | ✅      |
| `empty-lines`       | Limits consecutive blank lines                           | ✅      |
| `key-duplicates`    | Disallows duplicate keys in a mapping                    | ❌      |
| `truthy`            | Enforces explicit boolean values (`true`/`false`)        | ✅      |
| `document-start`    | Requires or disallows a `---` document start marker      | ✅      |
| `new-line-at-eof`   | Requires a newline at the end of the file                | ✅      |
| `comments`          | Enforces a space after the `#` in comments              | ✅      |
| `octal-values`      | Warns about ambiguous octal-style values (e.g. `0777`)  | ❌      |

**Lint all YAML files in a project:**

```bash
flak "**/*.yml" "**/*.yaml"
```

**Auto-fix issues where possible:**

```bash
flak --fix deployment.yaml
```

```bash
flak -f json "**/*.yaml"
```

**Fail the build if there are more than 5 warnings:**

```bash
flak --max-warnings 5 "**/*.yaml"
```

**Use a custom config file:**

```bash
flak --config ./configs/.flak.yml "**/*.yaml"
```

```bash
flak --rules indentation,trailing-spaces config.yaml
```

```
k8s/deployment.yaml
  3:1    warning  missing document start marker "---" document-start

✖ 3 errors, 2 warnings found across 2 files
```

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                      |
|------|----------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | No errors found                              |
| `1`  | One or more linting errors found             |
| `2`  | Warning threshold exceeded (`--max-warnings`)|
| `3`  | Invalid configuration or bad CLI arguments   |

```yaml
  - "*.generated.yml"

rules:
  indentation:
    enabled: true
    width: 2
  trailing-spaces:
    enabled: true
  line-length:
    enabled: true
    max: 120
  empty-lines:
    enabled: true
    max-consecutive: 2
  quotes:
    enabled: true
    prefer: single
  truthy:
    enabled: true
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  key-duplicates:
    enabled: true
  comments:
    enabled: true
    require-space-after-hash: true
```

### Rule Severity

Each rule can be set to `error`, `warning`, or `off`:

```yaml
rules:
  line-length:
    severity: warning
    max: 120
  key-duplicates:
    severity: error
```

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `indentation` | Enforces consistent indentation width |
| `trailing-spaces` | Disallows trailing whitespace |
| `line-length` | Enforces a maximum line length |
| `empty-lines` | Limits consecutive blank lines |
| `quotes` | Enforces consistent string quoting style |
| `truthy` | Restricts allowed boolean-like values |
| `key-duplicates` | Disallows duplicate keys in mappings |
| `comments` | Enforces comment formatting |
| `document-start` | Requires or disallows `---` document start marker |
| `new-line-at-end` | Requires a newline at the end of the file |

```
  line 17, col 5  error    wrong indentation (4, expected 2)  indentation
```

```yaml
some-key: some-value  # flak:ignore-line
```

## Overview

`flak` scans your YAML files for syntax errors, formatting inconsistencies, and common structural problems. It is designed to be fast, easy to integrate into CI/CD pipelines, and straightforward to configure.

```
$ flak config.yaml

config.yaml
  3:1   error    unexpected mapping key                  (syntax/mapping-key)
  7:12  warning  trailing whitespace detected            (style/trailing-whitespace)
 14:1   warning  line exceeds maximum length of 80 chars (style/line-length)

3 problems (1 error, 2 warnings)
```

---

## Installation

### Homebrew

```bash
brew install flak
```

### npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### pip

```bash
pip install flak
```

### From source

Requires Go 1.21+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest release for your platform from the [Releases page](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases).

---

## Usage

### Lint a single file

```bash
flak file.yaml
```

### Lint multiple files

```bash
flak file1.yaml file2.yaml file3.yaml
```

### Lint all YAML files in a directory

```bash
flak ./config/
```

### Lint recursively

```bash
flak --recursive ./
```

### Read from stdin

```bash
cat file.yaml | flak -
```

### Use in a pipeline

```bash
flak --recursive ./ && echo "All files passed!"
```

---

## Options & Flags

| Flag | Short | Default | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------------|
| `--recursive` | `-r` | `false` | Recursively lint all YAML files in a directory |
| `--config` | `-c` | `.flak.yaml` | Path to a custom configuration file |
| `--format` | `-f` | `stylish` | Output format (`stylish`, `json`, `compact`, `github`) |
| `--fix` | | `false` | Automatically fix auto-fixable issues |
| `--ignore` | | | Glob pattern(s) of files to ignore |
| `--max-warnings` | | `∞` | Fail if warnings exceed this number |
| `--quiet` | `-q` | `false` | Only report errors, suppress warnings |
| `--no-color` | | `false` | Disable colored output |
| `--version` | `-v` | | Print the current version |
| `--help` | `-h` | | Show help information |

### Examples

```bash
# Output results as JSON
flak --format json config.yaml

# Auto-fix fixable issues
flak --fix ./**/*.yaml

# Fail if more than 5 warnings are found
flak --max-warnings 5 ./configs/

# Ignore test fixtures
flak --recursive --ignore "**/fixtures/**" ./

# Use a custom config file
flak --config ./ci/.flak.yaml ./
```

---

## Configuration

`flak` looks for a configuration file in the following order:

1. The path provided via `--config`
2. `.flak.yaml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.yaml` in the user's home directory

### Example `.flak.yaml`

```yaml
# .flak.yaml

# Extend a built-in ruleset
extends: recommended  # options: recommended | strict | relaxed

# Files and directories to ignore
ignore:
  - node_modules/
  - "**/*.test.yaml"
  - dist/

# Override or configure individual rules
rules:
  # Disable a rule
  truthy: off

  # Enable a rule at warning level
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120

  # Enable a rule at error level
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2

  trailing-whitespace:
    level: warning

  comments:
    level: warning
    require-starting-space: true
```

### Extending shared configs

```yaml
extends:
  - recommended
  - ./shared/.flak-base.yaml
```

---

## Rules

Rules are grouped into the following categories.

### Syntax

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `mapping-key` | Detects duplicate or invalid mapping keys | ✗ |
| `syntax` | Validates overall YAML syntax | ✗ |

### Style

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `indentation` | Enforces consistent indentation | ✓ |
| `line-length` | Enforces a maximum line length | ✗ |
| `trailing-whitespace` | Disallows trailing whitespace | ✓ |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file` | Requires a newline at end of file | ✓ |
| `empty-lines` | Limits consecutive empty lines | ✓ |

### Structure

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `truthy` | Requires explicit `true`/`false` instead of `yes`/`no` | ✓ |
| `octal-values` | Warns on ambiguous octal values | ✗ |
| `key-ordering` | Enforces alphabetical key ordering | ✗ |

### Comments

| Rule | Description | Fixable |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `comments` | Enforces a space after `#` in comments | ✓ |
| `comments-indentation` | Ensures comments are indented consistently | ✗ |

> Run `flak --list-rules` to see all available rules and their default settings.

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No errors or warnings found |
| `1` | One or more linting errors found |
| `2` | One or more warnings found (only when `--max-warnings` is set) |
| `3` | Invalid configuration file |
| `4` | Unexpected runtime error |

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML files
  run: |
    pip install flak
    flak --recursive --format github ./
```

### Pre-commit

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/your-org/flak
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flak
```

Install the [flak VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/) for inline linting as you type.

```yaml
extends: default        # Start from the built-in default ruleset

ignore:
  - node_modules/**
  - vendor/**
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  trailing-spaces: error
  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  comments-indentation: error
  empty-lines:
    level: warning
    max: 2
  key-duplicates: error
  new-line-at-end-of-file: error
```

### Extending a shared config

```yaml
extends: "flak:recommended"
```

Available presets:

| Preset              | Description                                      |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `flak:default`      | Minimal rules for valid, parseable YAML          |
| `flak:recommended`  | Opinionated rules for clean, consistent YAML     |
| `flak:strict`       | All rules enabled at the `error` level           |

---

## Rules

Below is a summary of available rules. Each rule can be set to `"error"`, `"warning"`, or `"off"`.

| Rule                        | Description                                                  | Fixable |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `indentation`               | Enforce consistent indentation (default: 2 spaces)           | ✅      |
| `trailing-spaces`           | Disallow trailing whitespace on any line                     | ✅      |
| `new-line-at-end-of-file`   | Require a newline at the end of every file                   | ✅      |
| `line-length`               | Enforce a maximum line length                                | ❌      |
| `key-duplicates`            | Disallow duplicate keys within a mapping                     | ❌      |
| `truthy`                    | Enforce consistent boolean representations                   | ✅      |
| `comments-indentation`      | Require comments to be indented at the same level as content | ✅      |
| `empty-lines`               | Limit the number of consecutive empty lines                  | ✅      |
| `document-start`            | Require or forbid the `---` document start marker            | ✅      |
| `octal-values`              | Disallow ambiguous octal integer values                      | ❌      |
| `quoted-strings`            | Enforce consistent string quoting style                      | ❌      |
| `brackets`                  | Control whitespace inside flow sequence brackets             | ✅      |
| `braces`                    | Control whitespace inside flow mapping braces                | ✅      |
| `colons`                    | Enforce spacing around colons                                | ✅      |
| `commas`                    | Enforce spacing after commas in flow collections             | ✅      |

> 📖 Full documentation for each rule, including all available options, can be found in the [Rules Reference](https://github.com/your-org/flak/wiki/Rules).

### Check a Kubernetes manifest


```
  34:1   warning  line exceeds 120 characters (134)           line-length
```

```json
    "file": "deployment.yaml",
    "line": 12,
    "column": 5,
    "level": "error",
    "message": "wrong indentation: expected 4 but found 5",
    "rule": "indentation"

```


```
Fixed 1 issue in docker-compose.yml
```

### Use in a GitHub Actions workflow

```yaml

name: Lint YAML

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  flak:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install flak
        run: npm install -g flak
      - name: Lint YAML files
```

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml"
```

```yaml
ignore:

  empty-lines: warn        # Warn on excessive blank lines
  line-length:

  key-duplicates: error    # Flag duplicate keys as errors
```

| Level     | Description                              |
|-----------|------------------------------------------|
| `error`   | Fails the lint check (exit code `1`)     |
| `warn`    | Reported but does not fail by default    |
| `off`     | Disables the rule                        |

```yaml
  # Maximum line length
  line-length:
    level: warn
    max: 120

  # Require a newline at end of file
  trailing-newline: error

  # Disallow trailing whitespace
  no-trailing-spaces: error

  # Truthy values must be explicit (true/false, not yes/no)
  truthy: warn
```

### Rule Levels

Each rule can be set to one of the following levels:

| Level | Description |
|---|---|
| `error` | Fails the lint check (exit code `1`) |
| `warn` | Reported but does not fail the check |
| `off` | Rule is disabled |

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | No errors found |
| `1` | One or more errors found |
| `2` | Invalid configuration or unexpected runtime error |

---

## CI/CD Integration

### GitHub Actions

```yaml
- name: Lint YAML files
  run: |
    npm install -g flak
    flak "**/*.yaml"
```

### Pre-commit Hook

Add to your `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: flak
        name: flak YAML lint
        entry: flak
        language: node
        types: [yaml]
```

# flak

A fast, lightweight CLI tool for linting YAML files.

---

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Options & Flags](#options--flags)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Rules](#rules)
- [Examples](#examples)
- [Exit Codes](#exit-codes)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

---

## Overview

**flak** is a command-line linter for YAML files. It helps you catch syntax errors, enforce style conventions, and maintain consistency across your YAML configurations — whether you're managing Kubernetes manifests, CI/CD pipelines, Docker Compose files, or any other YAML-based configuration.

---

## Installation

### Homebrew (macOS/Linux)

```bash
brew install flak
```

### npm

```bash
npm install -g flak
```

### pip

```bash
pip install flak
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/flak.git
cd flak
make install
```

### Pre-built binaries

Download the latest binary for your platform from the [Releases](https://github.com/your-org/flak/releases) page.

---

## Usage

```
flak [options] <file|glob|directory>
```

Lint a single file:

```bash
flak config.yaml
```

Lint multiple files:

```bash
flak config.yaml docker-compose.yml
```

Lint using a glob pattern:

```bash
flak "**/*.yaml"
```

Lint an entire directory recursively:

```bash
flak ./config/
```

Read from stdin:

```bash
cat config.yaml | flak --stdin
```

---

## Options & Flags

| Flag                        | Short | Description                                              | Default     |
|-----------------------------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `--config <path>`           | `-c`  | Path to a custom configuration file                      | `.flak.yml` |
| `--format <format>`         | `-f`  | Output format (`text`, `json`, `github`, `compact`)      | `text`      |
| `--fix`                     |       | Automatically fix fixable issues                         | `false`     |
| `--stdin`                   |       | Read YAML input from stdin                               | `false`     |
| `--ignore <pattern>`        | `-i`  | Glob pattern of files to ignore (repeatable)             |             |
| `--no-color`                |       | Disable colored output                                   | `false`     |
| `--quiet`                   | `-q`  | Only output errors, suppress warnings                    | `false`     |
| `--max-warnings <number>`   |       | Fail if warning count exceeds this threshold             | `∞`         |
| `--rules <rule,...>`        | `-r`  | Enable specific rules (comma-separated)                  |             |
| `--disable-rules <rule,...>`|       | Disable specific rules (comma-separated)                 |             |
| `--version`                 | `-v`  | Print the current version                                |             |
| `--help`                    | `-h`  | Show help information                                    |             |

---

## Configuration

flak looks for a configuration file in the following order:

1. Path provided via `--config`
2. `.flak.yml` in the current directory
3. `.flak.yaml` in the current directory
4. `flak` key inside `package.json`

### Example `.flak.yml`

```yaml
# .flak.yml

extends: default          # Start from the default ruleset

ignore:
  - node_modules/**
  - dist/**
  - "**/*.generated.yaml"

rules:
  indentation:
    level: error
    spaces: 2
  line-length:
    level: warning
    max: 120
  trailing-spaces:
    level: error
  truthy:
    level: warning
    allowed-values: ["true", "false"]
  comments:
    level: warning
    require-starting-space: true
  empty-lines:
    level: warning
    max: 2
  key-duplicates:
    level: error
  document-start:
    level: off
```

### Extends

Use `extends` to inherit from a built-in preset:

| Preset        | Description                                    |
|---------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `default`     | Sensible defaults for general YAML files       |
| `strict`      | Stricter rules, all violations are errors      |
| `relaxed`     | Minimal rules, warnings only                   |
| `kubernetes`  | Opinionated rules for Kubernetes manifests     |

---

## Rules

| Rule                  | Description                                              | Fixable |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `indentation`         | Enforce consistent indentation                           | ✅      |
| `line-length`         | Limit maximum line length                                | ❌      |
| `trailing-spaces`     | Disallow trailing whitespace                             | ✅      |
| `truthy`              | Enforce consistent boolean representations               | ✅      |
| `key-duplicates`      | Disallow duplicate keys in mappings                      | ❌      |
| `empty-lines`         | Control the number of consecutive empty lines            | ✅      |
| `document-start`      | Require or forbid the `---` document start marker        | ✅      |
| `document-end`        | Require or forbid the `...` document end marker          | ✅      |
| `comments`            | Enforce comment formatting conventions                   | ✅      |
| `new-line-at-end`     | Require a newline at the end of the file                 | ✅      |
| `octal-values`        | Warn on ambiguous octal values                           | ❌      |
| `quoted-strings`      | Enforce or disallow quoting of string values             | ✅      |
| `braces`              | Control spacing inside flow mappings `{ }`               | ✅      |
| `brackets`            | Control spacing inside flow sequences `[ ]`              | ✅      |
| `colons`              | Enforce spacing around colons                            | ✅      |
| `commas`              | Enforce spacing around commas in flow collections        | ✅      |

Each rule can be set to one of three levels:

- `error` — Causes flak to exit with a non-zero code
- `warning` — Reported but does not affect exit code (unless `--max-warnings` is set)
- `off` — Rule is disabled

---

## Examples

**Lint all YAML files in a project:**

```bash
flak "**/*.yml" "**/*.yaml"
```

**Output results as JSON (useful for CI pipelines):**

```bash
flak --format json config.yaml
```

**Auto-fix fixable issues:**

```bash
flak --fix "**/*.yaml"
```

**Fail if there are more than 5 warnings:**

```bash
flak --max-warnings 5 "**/*.yaml"
```

**Use a custom config file:**

```bash
flak --config ./lint/.flak.yml "**/*.yaml"
```

**Disable a specific rule inline:**

```bash
# flak-disable-next-line truthy
enabled: yes
```

**Disable rules for a block:**

```yaml
# flak-disable truthy, quoted-strings
legacy_key: yes
another_key: unquoted value
# flak-enable truthy, quoted-strings
```

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning                                     |
|------|---------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | No errors found                             |
| `1`  | One or more linting errors found            |
| `2`  | Too many warnings (exceeded `--max-warnings`)|
| `3`  | Invalid configuration file                  |
| `4`  | Unexpected internal error                   |

---

```bash
cd flak

# Install dependencies
make deps

# Run tests
make test

# Run flak on itself
make lint
```

|-----------|-------------|
| `<Button>` | Clickable action element with variant and size support |
| `<Text>` | Typographic primitive for rendering any text node |
| `<Box>` | General-purpose layout container |
| `<Stack>` | Flex-based vertical or horizontal spacing utility |
| `<Divider>` | Horizontal or vertical visual separator |
| `<Badge>` | Small status or label indicator |
| `<Avatar>` | User or entity image with fallback initials |
| `<Input>` | Controlled text input with error and disabled states |
| `<Icon>` | Thin wrapper for rendering inline SVG icons |
| `<Spinner>` | Animated loading indicator |
| `<Tooltip>` | Accessible hover/focus content overlay |
| `<VisuallyHidden>` | Hides content visually while keeping it accessible |

---

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { Button, Stack, Text } from 'paw'

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <Text size="lg" weight="bold">
        Hello, paw 🐾
      </Text>
      <Button variant="solid" onClick={() => alert('clicked')}>
        Get Started
      </Button>
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

---

## Component API

### `<Button>`

```tsx
<Button
  variant="solid" | "outline" | "ghost"
  size="sm" | "md" | "lg"
  disabled={false}
  onClick={() => {}}
>
  Click me
</Button>
```

---

### `<Text>`

```tsx
<Text
  as="p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "label"
  size="xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
  weight="normal" | "medium" | "bold"
  color="inherit"
>
  Hello world
</Text>
```

---

### `<Box>`

```tsx
<Box
  as="div" | "section" | "article" | "main" | "aside"
  padding={4}
  radius="md"
>
  Content
</Box>
```

---

### `<Stack>`

```tsx
<Stack
  direction="row" | "column"
  gap={2}
  align="center" | "flex-start" | "flex-end"
  justify="center" | "space-between" | "flex-start"
>
  <Box />
  <Box />
</Stack>
```

---

### `<Divider>`

```tsx
<Divider
  orientation="horizontal" | "vertical"
  spacing={2}
/>
```

---

### `<Badge>`

```tsx
<Badge
  variant="solid" | "subtle" | "outline"
  color="neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"
>
  New
</Badge>
```

---

### `<Avatar>`

```tsx
<Avatar
  src="https://example.com/photo.jpg"
  alt="Jane Doe"
  fallback="JD"
  size="sm" | "md" | "lg"
/>
```

---

### `<Input>`

```tsx
<Input
  type="text" | "email" | "password" | "number"
  placeholder="Enter a value"
  value={value}
  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
  error="This field is required"
  disabled={false}
/>
```

---

### `<Icon>`

```tsx
import { ReactComponent as StarIcon } from './star.svg'

<Icon
  as={StarIcon}
  size={20}
  color="currentColor"
  label="Favorite"
/>
```

---

### `<Spinner>`

```tsx
<Spinner
  size="sm" | "md" | "lg"
  color="currentColor"
  label="Loading..."
/>
```

---

### `<Tooltip>`

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Helpful hint" placement="top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right">
  <Button>Hover me</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

---

### `<VisuallyHidden>`

```tsx
<button>
  <Icon as={CloseIcon} />
  <VisuallyHidden>Close dialog</VisuallyHidden>
</button>
```

---

## Design Principles

- **Primitive-first** — components do one thing and do it well
- **Composable** — combine primitives to build any UI pattern
- **Accessible** — ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation included by default
- **Unstyled-friendly** — bring your own CSS, CSS-in-JS, or Tailwind
- **Typed** — full TypeScript support throughout

---

## TypeScript

Every component ships with complete type definitions. No `@types/paw` package needed.

```tsx
import type { ButtonProps, StackProps } from 'paw'
```

---

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue before submitting a pull request.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/paw
cd paw
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

# tiny-date

Tiny, dependency-free relative date formatting for JavaScript.

Format dates like:

- `just now`
- `5 minutes ago`
- `2 hours ago`
